samples.summary: Share-link downgrade/revocation is enforced only in the client; with the Yorkie auth webhook in its default shadow mode the new revalidation bounds nothing against a non-cooperating client
samples.evidence: The added comment claims the 60 s re-resolution "bounds how long a revoked or downgraded link keeps the authority it was opened with" (shared-document.tsx:84-88, 1091-1106), and the docs/slides/notes rebuilds are the mechanism. But every one of those gates is client-side: `readOnlyDocStore` (packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:38-42) and the `MUTATING_METHODS` neutering (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4435-4448) both state in-code that they are the write boundary *because* the server-side check is off by default. The server-side check is `YorkieAuthController`, which computes the right decision (share role re-read per request, hasAccess() → `link.role === 'editor'`, yorkie-auth.controller.ts:213-217) but then discards it: `if (!this.enforce && !decision.allowed) { … return { allowed: true, reason: 'shadow' } }` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:111-119), with `enforce` defaulting to false (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101). Attack: a visitor given an `editor` link keeps the Yorkie client attached (the provider is not re-attached on downgrade) and keeps writing after the owner downgrades or revokes the link — either by holding a reference to the pre-rebuild store/editor or simply by not running the shipped UI. The revalidation raises the bar for an honest tab only; the claim in the comment is true only under `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`, which is not the default. Worth stating the precondition in the comment and/or making the downgrade path force a client detach/re-attach so a fresh webhook decision is taken.

samples.summary: Async continuations hold a pre-downgrade, fully writable editor/store; the readOnly rebuild does not neuter them, so a write can land after the role dropped to viewer
samples.evidence: `readOnly` is baked into an editor instance at construction — `insertImage` early-returns on the captured `readOnly` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4195) and the API-level neutering happens once at build time (editor.ts:4448-4470). The new deps list rebuilds the editor on downgrade (docs-view.tsx:590) and disposes the old one, but neither `EditorAPI.dispose()` (editor.ts:4400-4413, it only removes listeners/canvas) nor the newly added `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:651-655, which only drops the subscription and `onRemoteChange`) marks the object dead for writes. `insertImageFromFile` awaits `loadFileDimensions` and then the upload, then calls `editor.insertImage(...)` on the editor captured at drop time (image-insert.ts:135-137). Sequence: editor-role visitor drops an image → upload in flight → link downgraded to viewer → effect disposes the writable editor and mounts a read-only one → the upload resolves and the *old* editor writes the image inline into the live Yorkie document, past the permission that was just applied. The same shape exists for any other retained `EditorAPI`/store reference. The diff shows awareness of exactly this pattern (it added `if (this.disposed || this.pasting || this.readOnly) return;` to the clipboard resume, text-editor.ts:4261) but did not extend it to the editor/store handles the host keeps. Fix direction: have `dispose()` neuter the store's mutators (or set a `disposed` flag consulted by `EditorAPI` mutators) so a stale handle cannot write.

samples.summary: Revocation window is up to ~60 s, and the interval does not run while the tab is unfocused (`refetchIntervalInBackground` not set), so a backgrounded session can hold revoked authority indefinitely
samples.evidence: `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` (60_000) with `retry: 1` means a revoked or downgraded link keeps its authority for up to one interval plus the retry before the view closes. react-query does not run `refetchInterval` for a query whose window is unfocused unless `refetchIntervalInBackground: true` is set, which it is not (shared-document.tsx:1115-1118); `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` covers the refocus case, but a share session parked in an unfocused window keeps a `resolved` (and therefore a `readOnly`) that may be arbitrarily stale, while the Yorkie connection underneath stays attached and syncing. Since this client-side `resolved` is the write boundary in the default deployment (see the shadow-mode finding), the staleness window is the authorization window. Consider a shorter interval for `editor`-role links, `refetchIntervalInBackground`, or re-checking on user interaction.

samples.summary: The new share-link revalidation (the security control this change is built on) and the docs-view readOnly remount have no tests, while notes and slides both got one
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/` contains only `shared-document.tsx` and `shared-header-status.tsx` — no test anywhere covers the new `useQuery` revalidation: not that a revoked/expired link evicts the view (the `error || !resolved` fail-closed branch), not that an `editor → viewer` downgrade re-renders with `readOnly: true`, not that a transient failure is tolerated once. Likewise `docs-view.tsx` gained `readOnly` in its mount-effect deps (line 590) — the same permission fix the change wrote `slides-view-readonly.test.tsx` and `notes-view-readonly.test.tsx` for — but no equivalent docs test exists, so a future deps cleanup can silently drop the rebuild for the docs editor and every lane stays green. The lessons doc itself records "tests for the revalidation query" as deliberately skipped. Given the mechanical lanes only prove the suite is green, an untested permission gate is the weakest kind.

samples.summary: Misleading security comment: the added `readOnly` re-check cannot observe a permission change, because `readOnly` is fixed for the life of the TextEditor instance
samples.evidence: The new comment says `readOnly` "is read here, at the moment of the write, so the permission this session is allowed to exercise is the one that decides — not the one that held when the shortcut was pressed and the clipboard prompt went up" (text-editor.ts:4253-4260). But `private readOnly = false` (text-editor.ts:191) is assigned only in the constructor (text-editor.ts:719) and never mutated anywhere in the class; a permission change is applied by rebuilding the whole editor (docs-view.tsx:590), not by flipping this field. The re-check is harmless defence-in-depth, but the comment describes a dynamic authorization gate that does not exist, which is the kind of claim a later reader relies on when deciding a write path is already covered. Recommend restating it as "cheap consistency check; permission changes arrive as an editor rebuild".

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. shared-document.tsx:82-88 and 1091-1119 contain the claimed comment and the revalidation is purely a react-query refetch feeding `resolved.role` into `readOnly` props (lines 190, 331, 384, 434, 461, 749); the YorkieProvider/CollabDocumentProvider (1004-1077) are never detached/re-attached on downgrade, so no fresh server decision is taken. The write boundary really is client-side: packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:38-42 says so in-code, citing the webhook's shadow default. On the server, yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101 defaults `enforce` to false and 111-119 discards every deny, returning 200/allowed with reason 'shadow', even though hasAccess() (212-217) computes the correct viewer/editor decision. No alternative gate exists: the Yorkie token (auth.service.ts:66-80) carries identity only, no role, so nothing but the webhook can separate viewer from editor, and its 10m TTL only re-mints the same identity. Repo docs (docs/tasks/active/20260905-release-v0.6.9-todo.md:82-83) independently state shadow mode "allows every request regardless of the decision it computes". Real authorization weakness in-lane; no named refutation ground (not not-present, not already-guarded, not out-of-scope).

verdict.reason: Every element of the claimed chain checks out in the repo. `insertImageFromFile` awaits `loadFileDimensions` then `upload` before calling `editor.insertImage(...)` on the handle captured at drop time (image-insert.ts:135-137). `insertImage` gates only on the construction-time-captured `readOnly` (editor.ts:4195, param at 1036), and the API neutering allowlist runs once at build time under `if (readOnly)` (editor.ts:4448-4470), so an editor built writable stays writable forever. `EditorAPI.dispose()` (editor.ts:4382-4413) removes listeners/canvas/caches but sets no dead flag any mutator consults, and `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:651-655) only drops the subscription and `onRemoteChange` while retaining `this.doc`, so writes still land in the live Yorkie document via doc.insertImageInline -> store (model/document.ts:297-298). The host rebuilds the editor on `readOnly` change (docs-view.tsx:590, cleanup 549-577) but the in-flight drop continuation closes over the old writable editor (docs-view.tsx:491-493). The gate is load-bearing: editor.ts:4436-4439 and shared-document.tsx:1094-1097 state that with the default YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false this client-side readOnly IS the write boundary for a share-link visitor, and shared-document.tsx:88/1115 is the interval that performs the editor->viewer downgrade. The repo already applies exactly this disposed/readOnly re-check on the one other resuming write path (text-editor.ts:4261) but not here. No guard makes it unreachable; the finding is real and in the authorization lane.
